newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei's March futures surge to limit high.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei's March futures surge to limit high.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's March futures briefly surged by 1,000 points to the limit high on Monday.
The key March futures gained 1,000 points to 18,150 just ahead of the market close at 3.00 p.m. (0600 GMT).
The market's key barometer, the Nikkei average of 225 leading issues, soared 815.14 points, or 4.71 percent, to finish at 18,118.79.
Trade was volatile on Monday, with the index fluctuating by more than 1,000 points. It had briefly dipped to 17,019.56 early in the morning.
Its March futures briefly surged by 1,000 points to the limit high before closing at 18,130, up 980 points.
"Since last week's fall was so sharp, the index (at current levels) looked attractive and bargain-hunters emerged," said Keiko Kondo, a strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.

"But it is possible that the Nikkei 225 will fall again, as companies want to take profits before the end-March corporate book closings, and the market may see selling climax later in January or in February," Kondo said.
Turnover was heavy at 573 million shares, up from 411 million shares on Friday. Advancing issues beat decliners 944 to 232, while 104 issues were unchanged.

Brokers said that sectors such as banking and brokerages, which had been hit hard by growing concerns over their financial health and profit-taking before the book closings, bounced back on short-covering.
In other indices, the TOPIX index of all first section stocks jumped 46.08 points or 3.45 percent to end at 1,383.11.
The Nikkei 300 average closed 8.83 points or 3.47 percent higher at 263.19.

Brokers said the market was supported by a report by Jiji news agency saying the secretary-general of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, Koichi Kato, on Monday called on Taku Yamazaki, chairman of the party's policy-making committee, to come up with measures to deal with weak stock prices. But they added that the news, in itself, was unlikely to help the market break out of its malaise.
Analysts said the market would not take the comments seriously unless specific steps were proposed to make it certain that a sustained economic recovery would take place.
They said possible steps included a delay in a plan to increase Japan's sales tax from the current three percent to five percent from April 1 and cuts in budget spending.
By sector, gainers were led by sea transport, warehousing, fisheries, banking and securities.
The only major decliner was communications.
Sakura Bank Ltd soared 90 yen to close at 740 and was the most heavily traded issue with 17.05 million shares traded.

Sumitomo Bank Ltd gained 160 yen to 1,530 and was the second most heavily traded issue with 9.57 million shares changing hand. Fuji Bank Ltd ended 140 yen higher at 1,550. It had the fourth heaviest trade volume.
The second section index closed up 0.72 points at 1,734.34, with 8.21 million shares traded. The over-the-counter index was down 7.07 points at 1,273.02.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
